title: Phishing URL Analysis
description: Safely investigate suspicious links and identify credential harvesting sites.

slides.title: The Link is the Lure 🎣
slides.content:
# Why URLs are Dangerous

Clicking a phishing link can:
1.  **Steal credentials** via a fake login page.
2.  **Download malware** (drive-by download).
3.  **Track your IP address** and browser fingerprint.

**The Golden Rule for Analysts:** **NEVER CLICK THE LINK FROM YOUR WORKSTATION.** Not even in a VM on the corporate network.

**Safe Analysis Methods:**
1.  **URLScan.io:** Submit the URL. It renders a **screenshot** of the page using a remote sandboxed browser.
2.  **Browserling / Any.Run:** Interactive remote browsers.
3.  **Manual Defanging:** If you must share the link, **defang** it first.

slides.title: Defanging URLs 🛡️
slides.content: Replace `http` with `hxxp` and `.` with `[.]` to prevent accidental clicks.
slides.codeSnippet:
Original (DANGEROUS): https://login.paypal.com.secure-login.xyz/verify
Defanged (SAFE):     hxxps://login.paypal[.]com.secure-login[.]xyz/verify

# Also watch out for:
# - IP address URLs: hxxp://192[.]168[.]1[.]1
# - Data URIs: data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>
# - URL Shorteners: bit[.]ly/xxxxxx (Use 'Preview' feature or expand with CheckShortURL).

quizData.question: You receive a link: `https://www.paypal.com.security-update.info/login`. What is the actual domain?
quizData.explanation: The domain is the part right before the **first single slash** or the **last dot before the TLD**. Here, it's `security-update.info`. The `paypal.com` part is just a subdomain.

slides.title: Using URLScan.io for Safe Browsing 🖥️
slides.content:
# The SOC Analyst's Best Friend

**URLScan.io** is a free service that scans a URL and provides:
*   A **screenshot** of the landing page.
*   The **final destination** after redirects.
*   **DOM (HTML) content** of the page.
*   **Indicators** (e.g., "Login form detected", "Brand impersonation: Microsoft").

**Workflow for a Suspicious Link:**
1.  Copy the link from the reported email.
2.  Paste into **urlscan.io**.
3.  Click **'Make it Public'** (if safe to share) or **'Private Scan'**.
4.  Review the **screenshot**. Is it a fake Office 365 login page?
5.  Check the **'Indicators'** tab. Does it say 'Phishing'?
6.  Document the **URLScan.io report link** in your ticket.

**This provides conclusive evidence without touching the malicious site.**

slides.title: Identifying Typosquatting Domains
slides.content: Attackers register domains that look similar to real ones.
slides.codeSnippet:
Legitimate: microsoft.com
Phishing:   micr0soft.com (Zero instead of 'o')
            microsoft.net (Wrong TLD)
            microsoft-security.com (Added hyphen)
            rnicrosoft.com (RN looks like M)
            microsoft.co (Different domain)

# Tools to check domain reputation:
# - VirusTotal (Check the domain, not the full URL)
# - Whois (Look for newly registered domains - < 30 days old)

slides.title: The Redirect Chain 🔗
slides.content:
## Where Do You REALLY End Up?

Attackers use legitimate services (Google, LinkedIn, YouTube) as **redirectors** to bypass URL filters.

*Example:* `https://www.google.com/url?q=https://evil.com`

A basic filter sees `google.com` and allows it. But the user ends up at `evil.com`.

**Analysis:** Use URLScan.io or `curl -I` (from a cloud VM) to follow redirects and find the **final landing page**.
